items.title: Show HN: I made some transistor animations
items.raw_content: Hi HN, I made some animations of the most important kinds of transistors using my semiconductor simulation, details of which are on the page. I tried to make the visuals as realistic as possible while also aiming for clarity. If you want to go beyond the charge carriers and look at, for example, the electric field, you can do so in the simulation software. The desktop software also has less common devices like IBGTs and SCRs that have similar animations. The last thread about my software was posted here about a year ago: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43942279
items.title_zh: Show HN：我做了一些晶体管动画
items.summary: The author made animations of the most important transistor types with their own semiconductor simulation, aiming for realistic yet clear visuals, and notes that the desktop software also includes less common devices such as IGBTs and SCRs.

items.title: It's getting harder to focus every day
items.raw_content: I’m feeling it right now. I had to set a timer for 15 minute on my computer and block all distractions to write this. If I didn’t force myself to focus I would easily get distracted by something after few minutes. Even when I’m doing things that I’ve been waiting to do it, I still feel the urge to do something else. I don’t know how and when this happened. During the last few years I was always studying, working, and doing open source. And actually got stuff done. Doing all of those at the same time requires paying attention to what I wanted to do and ignore the noise.
items.title_zh: 专注正变得越来越难
items.summary: The author describes needing a 15-minute timer and blocked distractions just to write, and feeling the urge to do something else even during activities they had waited to do.

items.title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
items.raw_content: As I’m writing this, we’re in the middle of an AI-induced mass psychosis. People are literally token-maxxing themselves into hospital beds, scrambling to capture some of that market value before everything is automated away. I can’t blame them. Models keep getting better, programmers are being laid off left and right. We’ve been repeatedly told that AI will write 100% of the code by the end of the year. Whether that’s true or not, this may not be the best time to sit back.
items.title_zh: 如果编程已经被解决，为什么软件越来越糟？
items.summary: The author describes an AI-driven frenzy in which programmers are being laid off amid repeated claims that AI will write all code by the end of the year, and asks why software keeps getting worse.

items.title: Em dashes are amazing
items.raw_content: I fucking love em dashes. I spam them all the time. They make me feel free. I don’t give a shit what the “oh yeah let’s examine this piece of writing with a magnifying glass for any signs of AI” crowd thinks. I don’t give a shit that AI figured out how to produce em dashes before these online troglodytes did. Typing em dashes is not an AGI-complete problem. It’s not that difficult to produce an organic, artisanal, hand-crafted em dash — on Mac, for example, it’s simply Option + Shift + Hyphen .
items.title_zh: 破折号太棒了
items.summary: The author defends using em dashes freely, rejecting the idea that the punctuation is a giveaway for AI-generated writing and noting how to type one on a Mac.

items.title: Discrepancy-Rounded Fair Bandits with Static and Time-Varying Exposure Floors
items.title_zh: 具有静态与时变曝光下限的差异舍入公平老虎机
items.summary: The paper formulates stochastic bandits with exact exposure floors as a rounding problem and proposes BDQ-UCB, a blockwise algorithm that satisfies every time-varying floor deterministically with regret governed by the nonmandatory budget rather than the horizon. It provides matching lower bounds and extends the approach to overlapping group floors using Beck-Fiala null-space rounding.

items.title: Micro-Segmentation Anomaly Detection in Zero-Trust Software-Defined Network Fabrics
items.title_zh: 零信任软件定义网络架构中的微隔离异常检测
items.summary: The paper evaluates a Vision Transformer and a 1D-CNN for anomaly detection on raw versus micro-segmented network flow data from a simulated zero-trust SDN environment. Models trained on segmented input achieve higher accuracy and F1 (0.95 versus 0.90), with the ViT slightly better at recognizing lateral movement.

items.title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
items.title_zh: 并非所有大模型推理都能在思维链中看到
items.summary: The authors show that frontier models can use semantically irrelevant filler tokens to improve accuracy on synthetic reasoning tasks, with gains of up to 13 percentage points across 13 models. Filler tokens also let Claude Opus 4.5 satisfy a hidden modular arithmetic constraint without losing primary-task accuracy, indicating consequential computation with no interpretable trace in output tokens.

items.title: SAGE: Safety-First Defense-in-Depth Guardrails for Verified Lifecycle Control of High-Impact Generative AI
items.title_zh: SAGE：面向高影响力生成式 AI 生命周期受控验证的安全优先纵深防御护栏
items.summary: SAGE is an authorization-separated architecture that gates release of high-impact generative AI on catastrophic-risk admissibility, combining signed release manifests, detectors, risk envelopes, output checking, audit chains, and rollback, with formal verification of authorization separation. A vendor-symmetric study of 840 calls across GPT, Claude, and Gemini snapshots found low harmful-compliance estimates, with variation arising mainly from benign utility and safe redirection.

items.title: Hidden Boundary Motion in Transformer Optimization: Function-Space Orthogonalization of Affine Weight and Bias Updates
items.title_zh: Transformer 优化中的隐藏边界运动：仿射权重与偏置更新的函数空间正交化
items.summary: The paper shows that weight updates in affine layers contain a sample-independent component functionally indistinguishable from a bias update, termed boundary motion, and measures it dominating explicit bias updates in a four-layer Transformer trained on IMDb. A diagnostic optimizer, SBO-AdamW, improves validation accuracy in a single-seed experiment but suffers bias-coordinate drift, so the authors present it as evidence for the mechanism rather than a final optimizer.

items.title: Let AI Agents Translate Networks, Not Reason About Them
items.title_zh: 让 AI 智能体翻译网络，而非对其推理
items.summary: The authors argue that LLMs should be confined to translating network artifacts into formal logic while a solver handles reliable long-horizon reasoning, since such translation can be formally verified. They build TypoNet, which constructs and validates a symbolic model of an emulated production-scale WAN, and report faster, cheaper, and more reliable operational answers than an LLM, plus improved fault localization when used as a tool.
